$comment: Single source of truth for Beach Day decision logic. Every implementation (Hubitat/TRMNL, reTerminal firmware) must produce identical verdicts from identical inputs. Change a value here first, then regenerate the firmware constants (reterminal-e1001/tools/gen.py), update the Groovy and Liquid by hand, and note it in shared/README.md.

daylightWindow.$comment: THE one time window. Every aggregate that narrows by time uses the hours from that day's own sunrise to that day's own sunset, inclusive, as integer hours (sunrise 06:41 -> 6, sunset 19:52 -> 19). Today uses today's sun; tomorrow uses TOMORROW's sun. There is no separate beach-hours window.
daylightWindow.$comment2: Fallback applies only when that day's sunrise/sunset are unavailable.

inputAggregation.$comment: How each rule input is derived from Open-Meteo. Today and tomorrow are SYMMETRIC: the same calculation on the same kind of window, each using its own day's sunrise/sunset.
inputAggregation.precipProbability: max hourly precipitation_probability over that day's daylightWindow
inputAggregation.aqi: max hourly us_aqi over that day's daylightWindow
inputAggregation.aqiMin: min hourly us_aqi over that day's daylightWindow
inputAggregation.humidityMin: min hourly relative_humidity_2m over that day's daylightWindow
inputAggregation.humidityMax: max hourly relative_humidity_2m over that day's daylightWindow
inputAggregation.activeWeatherCode: mode of hourly weather_code over that day's daylightWindow; ties go to the LOWER code; falls back to that day's daily weather_code when the window has no rows
inputAggregation.hourlyRows: every hourly row in that day's daylightWindow as (hour, weather_code), in hour order; feeds the sun scan

sunnyWeatherCodeMax.$comment: WMO codes <= this count as sun: 0 clear, 1 mainly clear, 2 partly cloudy.

minSunHours.$comment: Minimum number of sunny hours (WMO code <= sunnyWeatherCodeMax) required within that day's daylightWindow for the forecast condition to pass. Guards against a single sunny hour at dawn qualifying an otherwise overcast day.

clearingDeadlineHour.$comment: The first sunny hour of the daylight window must be at or before this local hour to satisfy the forecast condition. 14 = 2 PM. This is a threshold on the hour, not a window boundary.

beachDayConditions.$comment: ALL must pass for a Beach Day. Operators are applied as: <metric> <op> <value>.

forecast.$comment: Passes when the daylight window has at least minSunHours sunny hours AND the sun is either the day's dominant condition or arrives by clearingDeadlineHour.
forecast.rule: sunHours >= minSunHours AND (activeWeatherCode <= sunnyWeatherCodeMax OR firstSunnyHour <= clearingDeadlineHour)

time.$comment: Current local time must be between sunrise and sunset minus this buffer. If sunrise/sunset are unavailable (0), this condition passes.

nightMode.$comment: When the time condition fails, the whole display flips to tomorrow's forecast and re-evaluates every condition against tomorrow's values.

states.$comment: Evaluated top-down; the FIRST match wins. Each entry's condition assumes all earlier entries did not match.

priority.title: Nice Day
priority.subtitle: But not quite beachy
priority.condition: temp >= 65 AND temp < 75 AND forecast condition passes
priority.$comment: Evaluated at the same precedence level as chilly_day (both gated only on beach/night/indoor/rain/wind not matching). temp ranges are disjoint, so they cannot both match.

parkingAlert.$comment: Street cleaning restrictions. When active, the alert replaces the sunset/time metadata line. Window opens at sunset the evening before the restriction day and closes at endTime on the restriction day.

activeWindow.opensAt: sunset on the day before the restriction day
activeWindow.$comment2: sunsetFallbackMinutes = 19:30 local, used when sunset is unavailable.

parkingAlert.textFormatNote: The start meridiem is dropped when start and end share it, e.g. '8-10AM'.

rounding.$comment: Displayed values are rounded ONCE, half-up, from the API value straight to an integer. Implementations must not round in two stages (e.g. to one decimal and then to an integer): 74.45 rounds to 74, never 75.
